sentences.zh: 十月，羹堯入覲，賜雙眼花翎、四團龍補服、黃帶、紫轡、金幣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Gengyao came to court for audience and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, the four-claw dragon rank robe, the yellow belt, the purple bridle, and gold coins.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gengyao came to the capital for audience and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, the four-claw dragon rank robe, the yellow belt, a purple bridle, and gold coins.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加一等阿思哈尼哈番世職，令其子富襲。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was given an additional hereditary ashan i hafan of the first class, and his son Fu was appointed to inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his service he was granted an additional first-class hereditary ashan i hafan rank, to be inherited by his son Fu.

sentences.zh: 羹堯才氣凌厲，恃上眷遇，師出屢有功，驕縱。

translations.literal: Gengyao was fierce and brilliant in talent; relying on the emperor's favor and repeated victories whenever his armies marched, he became arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and aggressive, Gengyao relied on the emperor's favor and his armies' repeated victories to grow arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 行文諸督撫，書官斥姓名。

translations.literal: In dispatches to governors-general and governors, he wrote their official titles followed by their personal names.
translations.idiomatic: In his communications to governors-general and governors, he addressed them by title and personal name—a deliberate slight.

sentences.zh: 請發侍衛從軍，使為前後導引，執鞭墜鐙。

translations.literal: He requested that Imperial Bodyguards be sent to accompany his campaigns, to march ahead and behind as guides, and to hold his whip and stirrups.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Imperial Bodyguards be detailed to his campaigns to march before and behind him as escorts and to hold his whip and stirrups.

sentences.zh: 入覲，令總督李維鈞、巡撫範時捷跪道送迎。

translations.literal: When he came for audience, he made Governor-General Li Weijun and Governor Fan Shijie kneel in the road to escort him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court for audience, he had Governor-General Li Weijun and Governor Fan Shijie kneel in the road to escort him in and out.

sentences.zh: 至京師，行絕馳道。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, he traveled along the forbidden imperial highway.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital, he rode along the forbidden imperial highway.

sentences.zh: 王大臣郊迎，不為禮。

translations.literal: When prince-ministers came to welcome him in the suburbs, he did not return the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When prince-ministers came out to the suburbs to welcome him, he refused to acknowledge the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 在邊，蒙古諸王公見必跪，額駙阿寶入謁亦如之。

translations.literal: On the frontier, all Mongol princes and nobles had to kneel when they saw him; when Prince Consort Abao came to pay his respects, he was treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, Mongol princes and nobles were required to kneel in his presence; even Prince Consort Abao was compelled to do so when paying his respects.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦陝西布政使胡期恆及景灝可大用，劾四川巡撫蔡珽逮治，上即以授景灝，又擢期恆甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: He once recommended Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner Hu Qiheng and Jing Hao as men fit for great employment; he impeached Sichuan Governor Cai Ting, who was arrested and put on trial, and the emperor at once gave the governorship to Jing Hao and promoted Qiheng to Gansu governor.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner Hu Qiheng and Jing Hao for high appointment. He impeached Sichuan Governor Cai Ting, who was arrested and brought to trial; the emperor promptly made Jing Hao governor and promoted Qiheng to Gansu governor.

sentences.zh: 羹堯僕桑成鼎、魏之耀皆以從軍屢擢，成鼎布政使，之耀副將。

translations.literal: Gengyao's servants Sang Chengdin and Wei Zhiyao were both repeatedly promoted for accompanying the army on campaign—Chengdin became a provincial administration commissioner and Zhiyao a brigade vice-commander.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao's servants Sang Chengdin and Wei Zhiyao were repeatedly promoted for serving with his campaigns—Chengdin rose to provincial administration commissioner and Zhiyao to brigade vice-commander.

sentences.zh: 羹堯請發將吏數十從軍，上許之。

translations.literal: Gengyao requested that several dozen officers and officials be sent to accompany the army, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao requested that several dozen officers and officials be detailed to his campaigns, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 覲還，即劾罷驛道金南瑛等，而請以從軍主事丁松署糧道。

translations.literal: On his return from audience, he at once impeached and removed relay station intendant Jin Nanying and others, and asked that Ding Song, a principal secretary who had accompanied the army, be appointed to act as grain intendant.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from audience he immediately impeached and removed Relay Station Intendant Jin Nanying and others, and proposed that Principal Secretary Ding Song, who had served on campaign, act as grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 上責羹堯題奏錯誤，命期恆率所劾官吏詣京師。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Gengyao for errors in his memorials and ordered Qiheng to bring the officials he had impeached to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Gengyao for errors in his memorials and ordered Qiheng to bring the impeached officials to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，珽逮至，上召入見，備言羹堯暴貪誣陷狀，上特宥珽罪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, when Ting had been arrested and brought, the emperor summoned him for audience; he fully recounted Gengyao's violent, greedy, and false impeachments, and the emperor specially pardoned Ting's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongzheng 3, Cai Ting was brought to the capital under arrest. Summoned to audience, he gave a full account of Gengyao's violence, greed, and false impeachments, and the emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 二月庚午，日月合璧，五星聯珠，羹堯疏賀，用「夕惕朝乾」語，上怒，責羹堯有意倒置，諭曰：「羹堯不以朝乾夕惕許朕，則羹堯青海之功，亦在朕許不許之間而未定也。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the second month, the sun and moon joined in one disk and the five planets aligned in a row; Gengyao submitted a congratulatory memorial using the phrase "xi ti chao qian." The emperor was angry, blamed Gengyao for deliberately inverting the wording, and instructed: "If Gengyao will not grant me 'chao qian xi ti,' then Gengyao's merits at Qinghai also remain unsettled, pending whether or not I grant them."
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the second month the sun and moon formed a conjoined disk and the five planets aligned in a row. Gengyao submitted a congratulatory memorial that used the phrase "xi ti chao qian" instead of the canonical "chao qian xi ti" (ever vigilant morning and evening). The emperor was furious, charging Gengyao with deliberately inverting the wording, and declared: "If Gengyao refuses to grant me 'chao qian xi ti,' then his merits at Qinghai remain for me to grant or withhold—and are far from settled."

sentences.zh: 」會期恆至，入見，上以奏對悖謬，奪官。

translations.literal: " Just then Qiheng arrived, was summoned for audience, and the emperor, finding his replies contradictory and absurd, stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Qiheng arrived and was summoned to audience; the emperor found his replies contradictory and absurd and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 上命更定打箭爐外增汰官兵諸事，不用羹堯議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that matters relating to increases and reductions of troops beyond Dajianlu be redetermined, and Gengyao's recommendations were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a reassessment of troop increases and reductions beyond Dajianlu, rejecting Gengyao's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 四月，上諭曰：「羹堯舉劾失當，遣將士築城南坪，不惜番民，致驚惶生事，反以降番复叛具奏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the emperor instructed: "Gengyao's recommendations and impeachments have been inappropriate. He sent officers and soldiers to build a city at Nanping, without regard for the frontier tribes, causing alarm and disturbances, yet he memorialized instead that surrendered tribes had rebelled again."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor declared: "Gengyao's recommendations and impeachments have been reckless. He sent troops to build a fort at Nanping without regard for the frontier tribes, provoking alarm and unrest, then memorialized claiming that surrendered tribes had rebelled anew."

sentences.zh: 青海蒙古饑饉，匿不上聞。

translations.literal: When the Mongols of Qinghai suffered famine, he concealed it and did not report it upward.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Mongols of Qinghai, he concealed the fact and failed to report it.

sentences.zh: 怠玩昏憒，不可復任總督，改授杭州將軍。

translations.literal: Slothful, negligent, and muddled, he can no longer be entrusted with the governorship and is instead reassigned as general at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Slothful, negligent, and muddled, he can no longer serve as governor-general and is reassigned as general at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」而以鍾琪署總督，命上撫遠大將軍印。

translations.literal: " Zhongqi was appointed acting governor-general and ordered to take charge of the Pacification General-in-Chief's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Zhongqi was appointed acting governor-general and ordered to assume the seal of the Pacification General-in-Chief of the Far Reaches.

sentences.zh: 羹堯既受代，疏言：「臣不敢久居陝西，亦不敢遽赴浙江，今於儀徵水陸交通之處候旨。

translations.literal: After Gengyao had been replaced, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant dares not remain long in Shaanxi, nor dares he hurry to Zhejiang; I now wait for orders at Yizheng, where land and water routes meet."
translations.idiomatic: After Gengyao was replaced, he memorialized: "Your servant dares not remain long in Shaanxi, nor dare hurry to Zhejiang; I now await Your Majesty's command at Yizheng, where land and water routes converge."

sentences.zh: 」上益怒，促羹堯赴任。

translations.literal: " The emperor grew even angrier and urged Gengyao to proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier and ordered Gengyao to proceed to his new post at once.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫伊都立、都統前山西巡撫範時捷、川陝總督岳鍾琪、河南巡撫田文鏡、侍郎黃炳、鴻臚少卿單疇書、原任直隸巡撫趙之垣交章發羹堯罪狀，侍郎史貽直、高其佩赴山西按時捷劾羹堯遣兵圍郃陽民堡殺戮無辜，亦以讞辭入奏，上命分案議罪。

translations.literal: Shanxi Governor Yiduli, Banner Commander and former Shanxi Governor Fan Shijie, Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Yue Zhongqi, Henan Governor Tian Wenjing, Vice Minister Huang Bing, Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Shan Choushu, and former Zhili Governor Zhao Zhiyuan submitted memorial after memorial exposing Gengyao's crimes; Vice Ministers Shi Yizhi and Gao Qipei went to Shanxi to investigate Shijie's impeachment that Gengyao had sent troops to surround a civilian fort at Heyang and slaughter the innocent, and they also submitted the findings for the record; the emperor ordered that the cases be deliberated separately.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi Governor Yiduli, Banner Commander and former Shanxi Governor Fan Shijie, Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Yue Zhongqi, Henan Governor Tian Wenjing, Vice Minister Huang Bing, Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Shan Choushu, and former Zhili Governor Zhao Zhiyuan submitted memorials one after another exposing Gengyao's crimes. Vice Ministers Shi Yizhi and Gao Qipei went to Shanxi to investigate Fan Shijie's charge that Gengyao had sent troops to surround a civilian fort at Heyang and slaughter innocents, and they too submitted their findings. The emperor ordered the cases deliberated separately.

sentences.zh: 罷羹堯將軍，授閒散章京，自二等公遞降至拜他喇布勒哈番，乃盡削羹堯職。

translations.literal: Gengyao was removed as general and given the idle post of clerk; from duke of the second rank he was reduced step by step to batulehafan, until all of Gengyao's offices were completely stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao was removed as general and assigned a vacant clerk's post; his rank was reduced step by step from duke of the second rank down to batulehafan, until every office and title had been stripped from him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，逮至京師，下議政大臣、三法司、九卿會鞫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was arrested and brought to the capital and referred to the Deliberative Prince-Ministers, the Three Chief Legal Offices, and the Nine Ministers for joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was arrested and brought to the capital and referred to the Deliberative Prince-Ministers, the Three Chief Legal Offices, and the Nine Ministers for joint trial.

sentences.zh: 是月甲戌，具獄辭：羹堯大逆之罪五，欺罔之罪九，僭越之罪十六，狂悖之罪十三，專擅之罪六，忌刻之罪六，殘忍之罪四，貪黷之罪十八，侵蝕之罪十五，凡九十二款，當大辟，親屬緣坐。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of that month the indictment was completed: Gengyao was charged with five counts of treason, nine of deception, sixteen of presumption and overstepping, thirteen of arrogance and insolence, six of usurpation of authority, six of vindictiveness, four of cruelty, eighteen of corruption, and fifteen of embezzlement—in all ninety-two articles—warranting death by decapitation, with relatives punished by association.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of that month the indictment was completed: Gengyao faced ninety-two counts in all—five of treason, nine of deception, sixteen of presumption, thirteen of arrogance, six of usurpation, six of vindictiveness, four of cruelty, eighteen of corruption, and fifteen of embezzlement—punishable by death, with associated punishment for his kin.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「羹堯謀逆雖實，而事蹟未著，朕念青海之功，不忍加極刑。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Although Gengyao's treason is real, the facts of the matter are not fully established; remembering his achievements at Qinghai, I cannot bear to impose the extreme penalty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared: "Though Gengyao's treason is real, the evidence is not fully established. Remembering his service at Qinghai, I cannot bring myself to impose the extreme penalty."

sentences.zh: 」遣領侍衛內大臣馬爾賽、步軍統領阿齊圖齎詔諭羹堯獄中令自裁。

translations.literal: " He dispatched Chief Imperial Bodyguard and Grand Minister Ma Ersai and Metropolitan Brigade Commander Aqitu to carry the edict to Gengyao in prison, ordering him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chief Imperial Bodyguard and Grand Minister Ma Ersai and Metropolitan Brigade Commander Aqitu to the prison with an edict ordering Gengyao to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 遐齡及羹堯兄希堯奪官，免其罪；

translations.literal: Xialing and Gengyao's elder brother Xiyao were stripped of office but exempted from punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Xialing and Gengyao's elder brother Nian Xiyao were stripped of office but spared punishment;

sentences.zh: 斬其子富；

translations.literal: his son Fu was executed by decapitation;
translations.idiomatic: his son Fu was executed;

sentences.zh: 諸子年十五以上皆戍極邊。

translations.literal: all sons fifteen years of age and above were banished to garrison the outermost frontier.
translations.idiomatic: all sons aged fifteen and above were banished to garrison the remotest frontier.

sentences.zh: 羹堯幕客鄒魯、汪景祺先後皆坐斬，親屬給披甲為奴。

translations.literal: Gengyao's retainers Zou Lu and Wang Jingqi were in succession executed by decapitation for their offenses; relatives were given out as bondsmen wearing armor.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao's retainers Zou Lu and Wang Jingqi were executed in turn; his relatives were distributed as bond-servants in the banners.

sentences.zh: 又有靜一道人者，四川巡撫憲德捕送京師，亦誅死。

translations.literal: There was also one called the Jingyi Daoist; Sichuan Governor Xiande arrested him and sent him to the capital, and he too was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Jingyi Daoist, whom Sichuan Governor Xiande arrested and sent to the capital; he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 五年，赦羹堯諸子，交遐齡管束。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Gengyao's sons were pardoned and placed under Xialing's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Gengyao's sons were pardoned and placed under Xialing's supervision.

sentences.zh: 遐齡旋卒，還原職，賜祭。

translations.literal: Xialing soon died; his original rank was restored and sacrificial rites were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xialing soon died; his former rank was posthumously restored and funeral rites were granted.

sentences.zh: 希堯，初自筆帖式累擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xiyao, at first starting from clerk of the Grand Secretariat, was promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Nian Xiyao began as a Grand Secretariat clerk and rose step by step to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 既，奪官，復起內務府總管，命榷稅淮安，加左都御史。

translations.literal: Later he was stripped of office, then reappointed Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, ordered to levy taxes at Huai'an, and given the additional title of Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Later stripped of office, he was reappointed Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, put in charge of tax collection at Huai'an, and given the additional title of Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為江蘇巡撫高其倬劾罷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was impeached and removed from office by Jiangsu Governor Gao Qichuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Jiangsu Governor Gao Qichuo impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 3.

sentences.zh: 胡期恆，字元方，湖廣武陵人。

translations.literal: Hu Qiheng, courtesy name Yuanfang, was a native of Wuling in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qiheng, style name Yuanfang, was a native of Wuling in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 祖統虞，明崇禎末進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong Yu passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong Yu received the jinshi degree late in the Ming Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 國初授檢討，官至秘書院學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty he was appointed reviser and rose to Academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he was appointed a reviser and rose to Academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父獻徵，自廕生授都察院經歷，官至湖北布政使。

translations.literal: His father Xianzheng, starting from a yinsheng appointment as clerk of the Censorate, rose to Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianzheng entered service through hereditary privilege as a Censorate clerk and rose to Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 期恆，康熙四十四年舉人。

translations.literal: Qiheng passed the provincial examination in the forty-fourth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng passed the provincial examination in Kangxi 44.

sentences.zh: 獻徵與遐齡友，歡若弟昆，期恆少從羹堯遊。

translations.literal: Xianzheng and Xialing were friends as intimate as brothers; in youth Qiheng kept company with Gengyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzheng and Xialing were close friends like brothers; in youth Qiheng kept company with Gengyao.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，獻詩，授翰林院典籍。

translations.literal: When the emperor made a southern tour, he presented a poem and was appointed Hanlin Academy registrar.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial southern tour he presented a poem and was appointed Hanlin Academy registrar.

sentences.zh: 出為夔州通判，有恩信，民為建生祠。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as subprefect of Kuizhou; possessing kindness and integrity, the people built a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed subprefect of Kuizhou, he earned the people's trust through kindness and integrity, and they built a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 羹堯為巡撫，薦期恆，遷夔州知府，再遷川東道。

translations.literal: When Gengyao became governor, he recommended Qiheng, who was transferred to prefect of Kuizhou and then again to Eastern Sichuan Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao became governor he recommended Qiheng, who was promoted to prefect of Kuizhou and then to intendant of the Eastern Sichuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 羹堯兼督陝西，复薦遷陝西布政使。

translations.literal: When Gengyao additionally supervised Shaanxi, he again recommended him for promotion to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao additionally took charge of Shaanxi, he recommended Qiheng again, and he was made Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 期恆通曉朝章國故，才敏，善理繁劇，羹堯深倚之。

translations.literal: Qiheng was thoroughly versed in court regulations and national precedents; quick in talent and skilled at handling complicated and urgent affairs, Gengyao relied deeply on him.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in court regulations and state precedent, quick-witted and adept at managing heavy affairs, Qiheng became someone Gengyao relied on deeply.

sentences.zh: 羹堯挾貴而驕，惟期恆能以微言救其失。

translations.literal: Gengyao, relying on his eminence, was arrogant; only Qiheng could by subtle words remedy his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao grew arrogant on his eminence, yet only Qiheng could check his excesses with quiet counsel.

sentences.zh: 羹堯奴辱咸陽知縣，期恆執而杖之，自是諸奴稍斂戢。

translations.literal: Gengyao's servant insulted the magistrate of Xianyang; Qiheng seized and caned him, and from then on the servants somewhat restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao's servant insulted the magistrate of Xianyang, Qiheng had him seized and beaten; from then on the household servants showed some restraint.

sentences.zh: 嘗諷羹堯善持盈，羹堯勿能用。

translations.literal: He once admonished Gengyao to know how to preserve fullness; Gengyao would not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: He once admonished Gengyao to preserve his fullness before fortune turned—but Gengyao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及羹堯敗，諸為羹堯引進者，爭劾羹堯以自解；

translations.literal: When Gengyao fell, all those whom Gengyao had brought forward vied in impeaching Gengyao to clear themselves;
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao fell, all those he had advanced rushed to impeach him to clear their own names;

sentences.zh: 期恆惟引咎，終不言羹堯，乃下獄頌系。

translations.literal: Qiheng only accepted blame on himself and to the end did not speak against Gengyao; he was then imprisoned and detained pending trial.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng accepted blame on himself alone and never spoke against Gengyao; he was imprisoned and detained pending trial.

sentences.zh: 至高宗即位，始得釋。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Gaozong acceded to the throne was he released.
translations.idiomatic: He was not released until the Qianlong Emperor acceded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 僑居江南，久之，卒。

translations.literal: He lived as a sojourner in Jiangnan; after a long while, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in exile in Jiangnan and died there many years later.

sentences.zh: 論曰：雍正初，隆科多以貴戚，年羹堯以戰多，內外夾輔為重臣。

translations.literal: The annalist says: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Long Keduo by virtue of imperial kinship and Nian Gengyao by the multitude of his battles became great ministers supporting the throne from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The annalist observes: At the start of the Yongzheng reign Long Keduo, by virtue of imperial kinship, and Nian Gengyao, by the weight of his battlefield victories, became the great ministers who buttressed the throne from court and camp alike.

sentences.zh: 乃不旋踵，幽囚誅夷，亡也忽諸。

translations.literal: Yet before they could turn on their heels, they were imprisoned and exterminated—perishing in what seemed an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet almost overnight they were imprisoned and destroyed—gone before anyone could fully grasp what was happening.

sentences.zh: 當其貴盛侈汰，隆科多恃元舅之親，受顧命之重；

translations.literal: When they were at the height of honor, extravagant and profligate: Long Keduo relied on his kinship as the emperor's maternal uncle and the weight of the testamentary command;
translations.idiomatic: At the height of their power and extravagance, Long Keduo relied on his status as the emperor's maternal uncle and the burden of the testamentary mandate;

sentences.zh: 羹堯自代允禵為大將軍，師所向有功。

translations.literal: Gengyao, having himself replaced Prince Yunti as commissioner-in-chief, found his armies victorious wherever they marched.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao had replaced Prince Yunti as commissioner-in-chief, and his armies won victory wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 方且憑藉權勢，無復顧忌，即於覆滅而不自怵。

translations.literal: Just then, relying on power and influence, without further restraint, they faced ruin yet did not themselves feel fear.
translations.idiomatic: Even then, trusting in their power without restraint, they showed no fear even as ruin approached.

sentences.zh: 臣罔作威福，古聖所誡，可不謹歟！

translations.literal: "Ministers must not presume to wield authority and dispense favors and punishments"—such is the ancient sage's warning; can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sages warned that ministers must not arrogate authority and dispense favors as they please—surely this is a lesson to heed!
